sub_domain: galaxy evolution and strong gravitational lensing
core_problem: The paper addresses the mass discrepancy in a massive compact quiescent galaxy at z~2, where the lensing mass implied by a complete Einstein ring is much larger than the stellar mass inferred from photometry, requiring additional mass in dark matter or a heavier stellar initial mass function.
methodology_summary: The authors identify a complete Einstein ring in JWST NIRCam COSMOS-Web imaging, model the lens galaxy with Sersic profiles, infer stellar population properties using Prospector SED fitting, and derive the total enclosed mass from the Einstein radius using photometric redshifts of the lens and source.
key_trade_off: The study confronts the tension between the directly measured lensing mass and the stellar mass estimated under a standard Chabrier IMF, forcing a choice between additional dark matter density or a bottom-heavy IMF to explain the missing mass.
limitations: Redshifts are photometric rather than spectroscopic, introducing uncertainty in the lensing mass estimate.
Stellar mass estimates depend strongly on the assumed initial mass function and stellar population synthesis models.
The dark matter mass is inferred using a fiducial decomposition rather than directly measured.
The result is based on a single galaxy, limiting generalizability.
Potential systematics in the Einstein radius and lens model remain untested with high-resolution spectroscopy or kinematics.
future_directions: Obtain spectroscopic redshifts for the lens and source with JWST NIRSpec to reduce mass uncertainties.
Measure stellar velocity dispersion and combine with lensing to break the dark matter versus IMF degeneracy.
Search for additional complete Einstein rings in wide-area JWST surveys to build a statistical sample.
Use high-resolution imaging and lens reconstruction to constrain the radial mass profile more accurately.
Look for IMF-sensitive absorption features in the lens spectrum to test bottom-heavy IMF scenarios.
research_gaps: Lack of secure spectroscopic redshifts for both lens and source in JWST-ER1.
No independent dynamical measurement of the lens mass distribution to complement lensing.
Uncertain contribution of dark matter versus stellar IMF variations in compact quiescent high-redshift galaxies.
suggested_title: Breaking the Dark Matter-IMF Degeneracy in Massive Quiescent Galaxies at Cosmic Noon with Spectroscopic Follow-up of JWST-ER1
suggested_abstract: We propose a spectroscopic and lensing follow-up program for the massive compact quiescent galaxy JWST-ER1 and its complete Einstein ring. JWST NIRSpec observations will secure redshifts for the lens and source and measure the stellar velocity dispersion, providing an independent dynamical mass estimate. Combining precise lensing, dynamical, and stellar population constraints will break the degeneracy between a bottom-heavy initial mass function and excess dark matter. Expanding this approach to a larger sample of complete Einstein rings in wide JWST surveys will reveal whether the mass budget discrepancy is common among massive quiescent galaxies at z~2.
